messages:
Kim (PM): Quick sync — product asked for a clear launch path for tenant isolation + multi-region routing. They want dates, gating criteria, and the minimal scoped playbook we can ship in Q3.
Arjun (Infra): +1. Need to decide whether routing policies are enforced at edge or at regional router. Tradeoffs: cost vs isolation.
Maria (SRE): Edge enforcement looks simpler for failover, but harder for per-tenant quotas. Regional gives better locality and billing breakdown.
Sophie (Eng): For Dedicated customers we already have PV-per-tenant idea. Private customers need VPC controls. We should separate "network isolation" from "routing policy" features.
Kim (PM): Customer ask summary: 1) per-tenant routing policies (latency vs cost), 2) geo-fencing for compliance, 3) predictable fallbacks for overload. They expect an enterprise checklist.
Arjun (Infra): Proposal sketch: Phase 1 (Q3): "Routing Policy DSL" + region preference header + soft-fallback to compatible model variant. Phase 2 (Q4): enforcement hooks at edge + tenant quota signals. Phase 3 (H1 next year): hard isolation lanes / tenant slices.
Maria (SRE): Launch criteria for Phase 1: automated test harness with synthetic traffic, perf regression <5% on p95 latency, fallback correctness tests. Also run a smoke with 2 pilot tenants.
Sophie (Eng): Spec snippet for the DSL (informal):
```
route {
  preference: [region:us-east-1, region:eu-west-1]
  policy: {latency: 0.6, cost: 0.4}
  fallback: {compatible_models: [gpt-small, gpt-quant], ttl: 60s}
}
```
Kim (PM): Nice. Need to map this to Console UI: route profiles, per-tenant defaults, and a way to pin region. Also add audit logs for routing decisions.
Arjun (Infra): Ops concerns: routing decisions add CPU at edge; add sampling mode first. Implement policy evaluation in a lightweight C++ lib used by edge/region.
Maria (SRE): Incident playbook: if region-level capacity drops below 20% we trigger cross-region failover window and notify on-call. Add canary for first 24h after policy rollout.
Sophie (Eng): Migration plan for existing tenants: 1) opt-in to route profiles, 2) 2-week observation window, 3) optional hard cutover. Document rollback path.
Kim (PM): Prioritization: customers with regulatory needs (EU financial + healthcare) get early access. Sales will provide list. Others on waitlist.
Arjun (Infra): Questions: Do we support tenant-level shard affinity? That adds complexity but improves cache hit rate. Recommend optional opt-in for Dedicated.
Maria (SRE): Perf target: when tenant affinity enabled, KV cache hit should improve by 15% in p99 token throughput for targeted workloads. Include metrics in rollout dashboard.
Kim (PM): Risk register: a) cross-region data egress costs, b) increased attack surface at edge policy engine, c) rollout rollback speed. Need mitigations.
Sophie (Eng): Mitigations: a) cost estimator in Console, b) default-deny for policy expressions, c) fast feature toggle with feature-flip in control plane.
deploy-bot: deploy started for infra/routing-policy-v1 on staging (build: 2026-03-21_08:12).
Kim (PM): Actions: Arjun -> tech spec + cost estimate by Mon; Sophie -> migration doc and DSL draft by Wed; Maria -> test harness and SLO checklist by Fri. I'll coordinate customer pilot signups.
Arjun (Infra): Ack. I'll include shard-affinity optionality and sampling mode in spec.
Sophie (Eng): Ack, will push DSL PR to repo and link in the doc.
Maria (SRE): I'll prototype the canary automation and add runbook steps.
Kim (PM): Thanks team — we'll present this to Product Council next Tuesday. :thumbsup:
Sophie (Eng): One more note: add a short-run internal benchmark comparing edge vs regional enforcement. Saves us argument later.
Kim (PM): Good call. Add it to Arjun's ticket.
